authorization.authorization_scope: Use the client-authorized shared production DAT login for read-only RateView discovery, testing, and on-demand operation with non-consequential or fictional shipment data. No application-level daily lookup cap applies. No other consequential DAT action is authorized.
authorization.approved_by: Jack (client approver and DAT account owner; surname and title TBD)
approved_environments: DAT production, limited to read-only RateView discovery and searches
authorization.production_use_constraints: Read-only RateView use with duplicate and uncertain-submission protection. Always respect DAT's own subscription, credit, usage, and rate controls and stop before booking, posting, messaging, purchasing/payment, deletion, or account changes.

workflow.name: DAT RateView lane pricing
workflow.business_purpose: Create a Playwright virtual employee that uses DAT RateView lane pricing as part of First Class Trucking's freight quote process.
workflow.trigger: On demand for the initial script
inputs: Origin, destination, and equipment type are documented by DAT as RateView search inputs
Any additional inputs DAT RateView requires; the exact UI field list remains TBD pending authorized observation and confirmation
outputs: Displayed market-rate range: low, average, and high
Displayed rate type, timeframe, per-mile value, and fuel information when available
workflow.existing_process_context: The existing CRM ingests quote emails. DAT is intended to provide carrier-side quote/rate data later in the freight quote process; the precise handoff is TBD.
workflow.expected_volume: Approximately 10 RateView lookups per day was provided as an expected volume, not a maximum
workflow.schedule_or_sla: On demand; latency target and support hours are TBD
success_metrics: Five consecutive successful read-only searches using fictional data
No duplicate or uncertain request is submitted again automatically
No booking, posting, messaging, purchasing/payment, deletion, or account changes
On authentication loss, pause for human reauthentication and resume from a safe pre-search checkpoint without duplicating a lookup or consuming an unintended extra lane credit

applications.name: DAT
applications.purpose: Obtain RateView lane pricing, including the lowest displayed rate and displayed market-rate information, for the freight quote process
applications.environment: Production, authorized for read-only RateView discovery and searches
applications.account_role: Client-authorized shared production login owned by Jack; exact DAT permission tier and RateView subscription are TBD. Shared use is a client-accepted operational/licensing exception pending the client's confirmation of DAT contractual compliance.

access.test_account_plan: Use the shared production login for read-only RateView searches with fictional data. Each live discovery or QA search requires its documented approval; the automation records usage without imposing a daily cap.
access.authentication_method: A human manually enters the client-authorized shared-login credentials. The automation does not store credentials or authentication artifacts.
access.sso_behavior: TBD; any SSO interaction remains human-controlled
access.mfa_behavior: Human-controlled only. The automation pauses and prompts for manual completion; it must not bypass or automatically handle MFA.
access.captcha_behavior: Human-controlled only. The automation pauses and prompts for manual completion; it must not bypass or automatically handle CAPTCHA.
access.session_constraints: Concurrent shared-login use is expected to invalidate sessions or cause logouts. On authentication loss, pause and prompt for human reauthentication, then resume from a safe pre-search checkpoint with duplicate and lane-credit protection.
access.secret_storage_method: Manual human entry only; no credential values or authentication artifacts may be stored in this project.
access.accepted_exception: The client has chosen a shared production login despite the documented individual-user constraint. Jack accepts the session invalidation/logout and licensing/contractual risk pending client confirmation of DAT contractual compliance.

sensitive_fields: Customer or quote context if displayed
screenshot_redactions: Redact commercially confidential data and all authentication information before storage or sharing
log_redactions: Redact commercially confidential data and all authentication information before storage or sharing
data_handling.retention_policy: Retain redacted screenshots and logs for 30 days, then delete them. Retention for any other evidence type and the exact deletion procedure are TBD.

consequential_actions.action: Execute a RateView lane lookup that may consume a lane credit
consequential_actions.approval_method: An authorized on-demand invocation approves one validated read-only lookup; discovery and QA continue to require explicit per-search confirmation
consequential_actions.automation_boundary: Before each search, verify the idempotency key and ledger state. Never automatically resubmit a completed, submitted, or uncertain request. Usage counts are audit-only and do not impose a cap.

consequential_actions.action: Booking, posting, messaging, purchasing/payment, deletion, or account changes in DAT
consequential_actions.approval_method: None; these actions are outside the approved read-only scope

acceptance_criteria: Complete five consecutive successful read-only RateView searches using fictional data
For each search, capture the displayed low, average, and high market range plus rate type, timeframe, per-mile value, and fuel information when available, together with the lookup timestamp
Record lookup usage for audit without imposing an application-level daily cap
Never perform booking, posting, messaging, purchasing/payment, deletion, or account changes
On authentication loss, pause for human reauthentication and resume from a safe pre-search checkpoint without duplicating a lookup or consuming an unintended extra lane credit
Keep credentials, authentication artifacts, and unredacted commercially confidential evidence out of the project
